title: Rewrite lint prober to Go plugin and add async release-scrub presubmit adapter
author: Mariela Santos
release_notes: Rewrite the presubmit lint prober as a Go plugin for lower memory usage and faster cold-starts; add an async release-scrub adapter to declutter stale release branches and reduce CI churn.
description:
Motivation: The existing lint prober was implemented as a TypeScript composite action that kept growing complexity and contributed to high memory footprints on ephemeral CI runners, and occasional flakiness when the lint matrix scaled. This PR rewrites the lint prober as a small Go plugin that runs as a native preflight process, reduces cold-start latency, and isolates plugin lifecycle from the composite GitHub action orchestrator. In parallel, it introduces an async 'release-scrub' presubmit adapter that runs after merge-window events to automatically detect and prune stale release branches/tags and remove obsolete presubmit caches. Goals: 1) reduce presubmit job runtime variance and memory usage; 2) decouple lint probing from Node runtime to avoid long npm install times on CI; 3) reduce CI noise from stale release artifacts and manual branch cleanup; 4) keep behavior backward-compatible for existing workflows. What I changed (high-level): - New Go module: infra/ci/probers/lint-prober (implements plugin contract used by presubmit runner). - New adapter: infra/ci/adapters/release_scrub (async task invoked by release hook dispatcher). - Updated GitHub Action composite to call the native binary when available, with fallback to the existing TypeScript shim (feature flag controlled). - Bumped a small set of dependencies (Go client libs and a couple of internal infra packages) and added a lightweight smoke test harness for the plugin. - CI/workflow updates: changed presubmit job to run the plugin under a short-lived container for faster cold starts and reduced matrix size for lint shards. Checklist: [x] Run local unit/integration tests for the Go plugin [x] Validate against canary repo with three sample PRs [x] Add feature flag (ci.use_native_lint_prober) and document migration steps [x] Add metrics and tracing spans (prometheus labels: "prober_type", "shard_id") [x] Add fallback and telemetry for failures (reported to Sentry) Commits (summary): - feat(ci): add go lint prober plugin and interface scaffolding - feat(ci): add release-scrub adapter and async dispatcher hook - chore(deps): bump github.com/google/go-github to v42.0.0, github.com/fsnotify v1.4.9 - test(ci): add smoke harness and small e2e test script - ci(workflows): switch presubmit to call native prober when flag enabled Small illustrative snippet (lint prober cmd wiring): """package main
func main() {
    prober := NewLintProber()
    exitCode := prober.Run(os.Args[1:])
    os.Exit(exitCode)
}
""" Changed areas (high level): - infra/ci/probers/lint-prober/* (new Go module, vendor + go.mod) - infra/ci/adapters/release_scrub/* (new adapter + tests) - .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (call native binary under ci.use_native_lint_prober) - .github/actions/ts-lint-prober/index.js (small shim retained as fallback) - tools/ci/smoke-harness/* (tests and Dockerfile) Migration notes: - Feature flag ci.use_native_lint_prober=false by default. Ops should flip the flag for canary repos first (eng/canary) and monitor metrics "lint_prober_success_rate" and runner memory. - Release-scrub is scheduled as an async job post-merge and will run in the release region queue to avoid contention with hot presubmit lanes. Observability: Added Prometheus metrics with the labels described above and tracing spans that tie into existing request/trace IDs. Also added an alert (SLO: presubmit-lint-latency P95 <= 60s) with a temporary relaxation window during rollout. Rationale and tradeoffs: - Go binary reduces Node.js startup and dependency install overhead on ephemeral runners but adds one more binary to distribute and validate in private deployments. The shim fallback ensures no regressions while rolling out. - The release-scrub adapter performs conservative pruning (only branches older than 60 days and no active PRs) to avoid data loss; audit logs are emitted. Review summary and conversation (condensed): - Ethan: "CI memory on presubmit dropped ~40% in canary runs, nice. A couple of minor nits on error messages and a missing unit test for the scrubber's dry-run path." - Author (Mariela): "Addressed both: clarified error text and added dry-run unit. Pushed fixup (see commit 3)." - Priya: "Why Go instead of Rust? We discussed performance and developer velocity in ENG-2201; go gives faster onboarding for infra team." - Liam: "Please ensure we have a rollback plan if the native prober starts failing at scale." - Author: "Added fallback and a feature-flagged rollout plan in the PR description and the ops playbook." CI and checks: - presubmit:lint (matrix) — initial run: 4/6 shards passed, 2 flaky failures (eslint remote rule, reran) - presubmit:go-tests — pass - smoke-harness:e2e — fail on first run due to race in adapter dry-run, rerun after fix — pass - release-scrub:integration — pass (dry-run mode) Final CI status: All checks passed. Merge outcome: Merged via squash on 2024-05-02 after 3 approving reviews. Post-merge actions: - Ops scheduled feature-flag flip for eng/canary on 2024-05-03 (observed drop in presubmit runtime). - Added a small migration job to upload the new binary to release artifact storage for private deployments. Files changed summary: 18 files, main additions in infra/ci/probers and infra/ci/adapters. Impact: Expected to reduce presubmit CI cost and runner churn by ~15-25% for typical repo activity, and to reduce manual branch maintenance effort through automated scrubbing. If problems are detected, revert is straightforward: flip ci.use_native_lint_prober -> false and revert the presubmit workflow commit. If you want to review the live canary results, metrics are in Grafana dashboard "CI/Presubmit/LintProber".
